evidence.text: The headword 匕 has a sequence labeled Shang, Western Zhou, Warring States, Qin, Shuowen small seal, and regular script. The entry calls 匕 a pictograph of an ancient shallow, long-handled food scoop with a somewhat pointed end, and cites Duan Yucai’s identification with a rice spoon. This is the book’s account of 匕 as a character in its own right; it does not independently establish that the early 比 graph contains 匕.

evidence.field: 比部; 比 headword and glyph sequence
evidence.text: The printed headword is 比. Its sequence labels Shang, Western Zhou, Shuowen ancient form, Qin, Shuowen small seal, Han, and regular script. The accompanying account says the main sequence retains a two-匕 construction from Shang–Zhou through small seal, with an exception among the ancient forms, and says clerical transformation straightened the strokes and obscured their pictorial quality. These are 董莲池’s analyses, not an independently settled account of the early graphs.

evidence.field: 比部; 董莲池’s formation, component-role, and semantic proposals
evidence.text: The entry proposes an ideographic construction from two 匕 signs, described as ancient shallow, long-handled food scoops. It says placing the two signs in parallel conveys adjacency or nearness and explicitly says 匕 also cues the pronunciation. It accepts the sense of Shuowen’s gloss 密也 while rejecting Shuowen’s analysis as two 人 forms reversed from 从. It proposes semantic extensions from nearness to union, factional association, and comparison. These are attributed proposals, not independently established formation or semantic chronology.

evidence.field: 比部; cited examples and proposed senses
evidence.text: The entry cites 《詩·周頌·良耜》其比如栉 for its adjacency sense; an oracle-bone phrase 王比望乘伐下危 for union; 《論語·為政》君子周而不比 for factional association; and 《左傳·昭公二十八年》 for comparison. This records the author’s interpretation and examples; it does not establish a dated chain of semantic development or independently verify the oracle-bone graph.

evidence.field: 比; distinct Middle Chinese and Old Chinese entries
evidence.text: The table lists 比 bǐ, MC pjijX, OC *C.pijʔ, gloss “compare,” and separately 比 bì, MC pjijH, OC *pij-s, gloss “combine; all” (GSR 0566g). Relative to 匕 *pijʔ in the same system, the bǐ entry shares rhyme and coda but has the additional onset notation *C-. Similarity alone does not establish that 匕 functions as a phonetic component in 比.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong, 比 entry
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; competing graph analysis and early uses
evidence.text: The entry analyzes oracle-bone and bronze 比 as two 人 forms placed side by side and distinguishes 比 from 从 by the figures’ usual orientation and 比’s more curved lower part, attributing the distinction to 屈萬里. It also reports oracle-bone readings as 妣 and an “assist/support” interpretation of 王比望乘 attributed to 李宗焜. This account conflicts with 字源’s two-匕 proposal; the page reports scholarly interpretations rather than independently resolving the graph identity.

evidence.source: 李宗焜, “卜辭中的「望乘」——兼釋「比」的辭意,” 《古文字與古代史》第一輯 (2007), p. 117; Academia Sinica abstract
evidence.field: Early Shang phrase 王比望乘; competing lexical interpretations
evidence.text: The abstract reports earlier readings of 比 in 王比望乘 as “follow” or “lead,” and an alliance reading. Li argues instead for “assist/support,” potentially by gathering people and materials for a campaign. This substantiates disagreement over the phrase’s interpretation, not a settled general semantic history for 比.

The early oracle-bone and bronze specimens were not individually inspected in this research pass. The book’s two-匕 analysis and the person-form accounts remain attributed, competing interpretations; the scan sequence alone does not settle the signs’ identity or referent.

The cited book’s semantic proposals are not a dated chronology. The exact relationship between the Shang use and adjacency, association, assistance, and comparison remains unresolved; the phrase 王比望乘 has competing readings in the inspected scholarship.
